segments.text: Hey friends, I can’t tolerate this anymore.
I’m going to quit this job.
Aman’s friend was shocked to hear this, because just four months
ago, Aman had requested him a lot and got this job through his recommendation.
It wasn’t that Aman was a lazy guy.
He was a 26-year-old, very hardworking, kind-hearted boy.
Vikram asked, “Bro, what’s the problem?” He said, “It’s the same office
politics that happened at my previous workplace too.
These people constantly
target me and speak ill of me, and all this is mentally exhausting for me.
To stay away from all this,
I often start using my phone, but the phone itself is a very big trap.
While using it, I get so distracted that I’m unable to do my work properly.”
The manager keeps scolding me, the work pressure just keeps increasing, and
because of all
this, I’m neither able to perform well, nor is my mental health in a good state.
I’m not earning much money, my performance isn’t improving, and there’s no growth.
That’s why now I’ll quit this job for sure, man.
Vikram says, “Something
similar happened with you in your previous office too, right?” Aman says, “Yes,
I don’t know why all these things keep happening to me again and again.
I try very hard not to get involved in all this, but people
still pull me into office politics.
That’s why now I
want to get away from all of it.” Vikram could understand the depth of the problem.
That’s why he said to Aman, “Aman, you’ll need to consult a doctor.” Aman said,
“Bro, I’m not going crazy.
Yes, my mental health isn’t good, but it hasn’t come to the point where I need
to see a doctor.” Vikram replied, “Bro, I’m not talking about that kind of doctor.
I know a doctor who is more of a philosophical doctor—a doctor for life.
He has helped me a lot in moving forward in my own life too.”
“I want you to meet him once before quitting the job.
Today, I’ve reached a senior position in this company because of him.
I really think you should talk to him at least once.”
Before taking any big decision, Aman hesitates a little, but then agrees.
A few days later, he reaches the address that
Vikram had given him. The place was far from the city.
It was a lovely bungalow, with a river flowing beside it.
There were lots of bushes and trees around—giving it a
complete farmhouse-like feel.
He knocks and goes inside the house, and what he sees is that the entire place
is filled with books.
In front of him stands a young man wearing glasses.
Aman asks, “Are you Dr.
Book?” Smiling, he says, “Yes, Vikram has sent you, right?
Come, have a seat in this room.” Aman finds it very fascinating—so many
books, something he has never seen before in his life. At one point, Dr.
Book says, “Don’t worry, I’m not going to make you read all these books.
Tell me, what’s your problem?” Aman is still observing the environment
around him.
But then his job and all his problems come to his mind, and he starts telling Dr.
Book everything, one by one. After listening to all this, Dr.
Book says, “Wait here for a
minute,” and goes inside. Nearby, there is a special kind of cabinet.
From inside it,
he says, “Look, this cabinet has a collection of my most precious books.
One of these books will help you a lot.” “Do you want me to help you?” Aman
says, “Sir, that’s exactly why
I’ve come here.” “Alright,” he says as he takes out a book.
“Today, I’ll share five lessons from this book with you.
But I won’t share these lessons casually.
I want you to understand them properly and
remember them, so that these problems never come back into your life again.”
“That’s why I’ll explain the lessons from this book to you in the form of a story.
Do you like stories?” Aman replied, “Yes.
If it’s a good story, why not? “Alright,” Dr. Book says.
“Look, you may have heard this story before, but the way I’m going to tell it
to you today, you’ve never heard it like this—because this is not just a story.
Hidden within this story are five lessons from this amazing book, lessons
that have the power to eliminate your life’s problems from the root.”
“But I want you to listen to this story very carefully
and try to figure out for yourself what those five lessons are.
This story is very similar to your own life, so listen closely.”
Aman agrees, and from there the story begins. The story is 300 years old.
It is about a monk who lived in a monastery in the mountains.
He wanted to become a great monk.
He wanted to gain knowledge and understand many things.
But the problem was that he was disturbed.
The people around him used to play a lot of politics and say things he didn’t like.
Because of this, he couldn’t focus or even meditate properly.
So he decided that he would leave this monastery and go
to another one. The problem was that changing a monastery wasn’t so easy.
Still, he somehow reached the head monk and said to him, “I don’t like
the environment here at all.
When I came here, I thought everyone would be good, calm, and positive.
But the environment here is not what I expected or what
I need.” After listening to all this, the head monk said, “Alright.
Normally this isn’t allowed, but I’ll accept your request on one condition.”
The young monk said,
“Okay, please tell me—what do I have to do?” He replied, “Nothing much.
Do you see this spoon?
I’ll put ten drops of water in it.
You have to keep this spoon in your mouth, take one round of the monastery, and
then come back to me.” “If even a single drop falls, I won’t accept your request.
But if you come back to me without spilling even one drop,
I’ll fulfill your request.” The young monk was very confident.
He thought, *I’ve done much harder things here.* He had already endured physical
pain and completed many tough tasks before. There he said, “This will be a
piece of cake for me.” He takes the spoon, and they put ten drops of water in it.
Then he starts walking. Since he is a bit overconfident, he starts
taking fast steps.
At first, for the first one or two steps, he walks comfortably.
But then suddenly, he feels a little nervous. He becomes a little careless,
and after just a few steps, a few drops of water fall from the spoon.
He thinks, *The chance is lost.* Feeling disappointed, he looks at the head monk,
who, smiling, says, “I’ll give you one more chance.” After this, the monk refills
the spoon with water, and this time, he starts walking slowly and carefully.
He doesn’t panic.
But then he notices that the other monks around are laughing at him.
As soon as he sees them, his focus breaks, and a little water spills
from the spoon again.
When it spills, he gets very angry.
He thinks about shouting at the other monks and scolding them, but the head monk
is watching, and seeing this, he gestures
him to calm down. He refills the spoon with water again.
This time, he starts taking his steps very slowly and
doing everything so carefully that he begins to feel bored.
Just as he is getting bored, his attention suddenly goes back to a few people
who are making faces at him, laughing, and calling him crazy. Seeing this,
he gets so angry that his mouth trembles, and water spills from the spoon again.
He becomes extremely frustrated, but since
the head monk is watching, he controls his anger and steadies himself.
The head monk then gestures toward him and says, “This is your
last chance.” Hearing this, he breaks out in a cold sweat.
He fills the spoon with water one last time and starts walking again.
He takes a deep breath and thinks that no matter what, he has
to leave this place, so now he won’t let anything distract him.
He carefully
adjusts his technique, placing his feet very slowly, and keeps his full focus
on the water and the spoon. Many people around, who always make fun
of him, are mocking him again, but still his full focus remains on the spoon.
This time, he feels very bored.
His arms and legs start to ache strangely, but he completes the entire circle
this time.
Happily, he goes to the head monk and says, “See, sir, yes, it took two or three
tries, but I did it.” “But I did it, and not a single drop fell.” Then the
head monk, smiling, looks at the young monk and asks, “When you were walking
in this final round, did you hear any of the politics around you?” The young
monk says, “No.” And he realizes what the head monk was trying to teach him.
Now, after the story, Dr.
Book asks Aman, “Did you
understand the story?” Aman smiles and says, “Yes, I understood the story.” Dr.
Book asks, “What did
you understand?” Aman replies, “I need to keep my focus on my own work.
If I stay focused on my work, the outside world won’t affect me.” Dr.
Book says, “Yes, that is the core theme.” “This story has a very big lesson.
But there were five more lessons hidden in it.
Do you understand what they were?” Now Aman says, “No.
I understood at least that I need to focus, but I’m not able to focus.
That’s the problem.” Dr.
Book says, “Now
I’m going to tell you the five lessons that were hidden in this story.
These are also the answers to your question about how to focus.” Lesson No.
1: Focus is not a talent; it’s a skill.
When the young monk went for the first time, he was confident that
he could do this simple task.
The first time he failed. The second time he failed.
The third time he failed too.
But on the fourth attempt,
he was finally able to do it successfully, giving his full attention to the task.
Similarly, you must remember this too. Focus is not a talent;
it’s a skill that gets better the more you practice it.
The second distraction isn’t outside—it’s inside.
When the monk was walking the second time, people were laughing at him.
Even the third time, it happened.
By the fourth time, he decided that the outside distractions weren’t the problem.
The real distraction was inside—his own mind, which kept pulling his attention
toward them again and again. And that’s why he succeeded on the fourth attempt.
Lesson number three: Depth creates results, not speed.
When the monk was walking for the first time, he didn’t have the right technique.
He was just trying to walk however he thought he should.
But after doing it two or three times, he changed his technique and brought depth
into the task he was performing. Many times, we try to do things very quickly.
But whenever you try to do things in a hurry, without depth,
even if you succeed, it won’t be true success.
Lesson No. 4: Rituals are stronger than willpower.
Using the same spoon, the same water, the same path, and practicing
repeatedly—that is a kind of ritual. Rituals help people focus.
They help in building skills, and the *Deep Work* book also
says that you need to create certain rituals for yourself.
Lesson No. 5: Boredom is necessary for focus.
When the monk failed the first time, it was because of his wrong technique.
But by the third time, he started getting bored, and that boredom also
made him easily distracted. But on the fourth attempt, instead
of running away from boredom, he made it his friend.
Because of this, he was able to complete the entire round.
Look, Aman, anyone who runs away from boredom can never do deep work.
You also need to understand these lessons.
Politics, people’s
comments, distractions from your phone—no matter where you go, these will
always be with you. Until you understand these five lessons and actually follow
them, no matter how many offices you change, you won’t be able to move forward.
This is exactly what I once explained to Vikram as well.
The day he understood this, his life changed.
Politics was the same for Vikram too, but today he is the company’s Vice President,
and that’s why he sent you to me. You also need to understand this very well.
You have to apply these five lessons and create a ritual.
Aman asks, “But how can I create a ritual for all this?” Dr.
Book says, “Don’t worry.
Every week,
I hold a meeting with young, talented, hardworking people like you—people who can
achieve a lot in life—and in that meeting, we practice these lessons together.”
“If you want, we can practice these things together.” Aman says, “Of course.
Why not, sir?
I would love to do this important work with you and Vikram.” After this, Aman and
Vikram met every week for three months to practice focus, spending half an hour
to an hour working together with full concentration.
They followed a project-work ritual that Dr.
Book had created, so they could learn to treat focus not as a
talent, but as a skill.
There, they worked on tasks that required depth
rather than speed, and they deliberately allowed themselves to experience boredom.
The result was that, gradually, Aman—who used to get irritated by people’s comments
very quickly and get angry—began
to change. He used to get distracted repeatedly by using his mobile.
Now, he even stopped touching his phone.
Within six months, he accomplished more work than his entire team.
People were noticing all these changes.
Even Aman’s boss noticed, and seeing this, he promoted him to team manager.
Now look, friends, this was not just a story—this story contained
five powerful lessons from the *Deep Work* book.
If you want, just like Dr.
Book made Aman practice, I can also teach you how to develop the ability to focus.
If you want to learn, create a ritual, and work with depth, I would
like to invite you to do so. I’m doing a live session for you all, which I usually
do every Sunday.
And what’s the cost of this?
Well, for now, I’ve set the cost at zero rupees.
There’s a bonus included, but the bonus is only for those who are my 99-rupee
Summary Board subscribers.

This way, even if you don’t get time to read the book,

And what I really want is for you to not just buy the subscription and forget about

that we can actually apply the lessons from those books in real life.
So, if you want to apply the lessons from *Deep

I’ll keep sharing all the details there—when the live will happen,

And if you want to keep learning the lessons from such books in story
